cultural-landscape.def: The land as people have changed it: buildings, fields, roads, signs and places of worship laid over the physical landscape.

sequent-occupance.def: The idea that each group that lives in a place leaves marks on the landscape that later groups keep, change or reuse, so the landscape has layers.

postmodern-architecture.def: A building style from about the 1970s on that mixes older and newer styles on purpose, often with playful shapes; it looks similar in cities around the world.

traditional-architecture.def: Buildings made in a long-standing local style, usually with local materials, such as adobe homes in New Mexico or thatched cottages in Ireland.

ethnic-neighborhood.def: An area within a city or town where many people of one ethnic group live, often marked by their language on signs, their shops and their places of worship.

ethnicity.def: Identity with a group of people who share ancestry, history and cultural traditions. It is cultural, not biological.
